title: Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Ice melts on a warm afternoon, yet the same water freezes in a freezer. Only the temperature changed. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 5, Thermodynamics) Aarav drops ice into his water bottle and we find one number about the reaction alone that predicts its direction and where it stops.

You will see enthalpy and entropy as two teams in a tug of war, then turn a temperature knob on the molecule bench: for melting ice (Delta H = +6.01 kJ/mol, Delta S = +22.0 J/K/mol) enthalpy wins at -10 C, the teams tie at 273 K, and entropy wins at 25 C. The score is the Gibbs energy, Delta G = Delta H - T Delta S, derived step by step from the total entropy. We cover the four sign cases, the link to equilibrium, Delta G naught = -RT ln K = -2.303 RT log K with R = 8.314 J/K/mol, work out NCERT's oxygen to ozone example (+163 kJ/mol), show the unit trap, then an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 57 of our PUC Chemistry series, and the last episode of Chapter 5.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
